last_report.message: module.py replaces the summing stub with a validated ledger implementing solve(data) per the contract. Checks run in order: kind, amount (int >= 1, bools rejected), hold id uniqueness or release id existence, then available-funds check for debit and hold. Credit, debit, hold, and release update balance and held as specified, and the input is not mutated. run_tests passed the 3 public cases (empty ops, credit/debit, credit/hold), with input_mutated false. Only the public tests were run, so hidden edge cases are unverified. Unhashable id values (e.g. lists) would raise TypeError rather than ValueError; the contract doesn't cover this. test_cases.json was not part of the allowed files, so no receipt bound to it was produced.

content.assignment: Write module.py (stdlib only, no I/O, no dynamic code execution) exposing solve(data). Implement this contract exactly. Input: data is a dict with key "ops", a list of operation objects. Each operation has "kind" and, depending on kind, "amount" and/or "id". Apply operations in order and return {"balance": int, "held": int, "available": int}, where available = balance - held. Per operation, check rules in this exact order and raise ValueError on the first failure (no result is returned): (1) kind must be one of credit, debit, hold, release; otherwise ValueError. (2) For credit, debit, hold: amount must be an integer >= 1; booleans are not integers here and raise ValueError. (3) For hold: id must not already name an active hold. For release: id must name an active hold. Violation raises ValueError. (4) For debit and hold: amount must not exceed currently available funds (balance - held), else ValueError. Effects: credit increases balance by amount. debit decreases balance by amount. hold adds an active hold of amount under id (held increases by amount; balance unchanged). release removes the hold named by id, decreasing held by that hold's amount, and ignores any amount field. An empty ops list returns {"balance":0,"held":0,"available":0}. Do not mutate the input. Replace the current module.py, which is wrong (it sums amounts and ignores kinds, holds, and validation). Write only module.py.
content.user_contract: Implement solve(data) for {"ops": list of operations}. Each operation is an object with "kind" and, depending on kind, "amount" and/or "id". Apply the operations in order and return {"balance": int, "held": int, "available": int} where available is balance minus held. Rules, checked in exactly this order for each operation: (1) "kind" must be one of credit, debit, hold, release; anything else raises ValueError. (2) For credit, debit and hold, "amount" must be an integer of at least 1; otherwise ValueError. Booleans are not integers here and raise ValueError. (3) For hold, "id" must not already name an active hold; for release, "id" must name an active hold; a violation raises ValueError. (4) For debit and hold, "amount" must not exceed the currently available funds; otherwise ValueError. credit increases balance. debit decreases balance. hold adds an active hold of amount under id. release removes the hold named by id and ignores any "amount" field. The first failing operation raises and no result is returned. An empty operation list returns zeros. Do not mutate the input.
